findings.title: Central model-aware algorithm is undefined at its specified first step
findings.source_claim: Operational model-aware factor for dynamic preference optimization from identical SFT policy/reference initialization
assumptions_verified: Positive preferred/rejected probabilities and finite log ratios
Zero running mean specified after Eq. (14)
Normalization called before the first gradient/state update
Reported N, K, beta and momentum

supporting_count_error.scope: Separate finite positive-state arithmetic, not an assertion that the undefined startup reaches it
supporting_count_error.standalone_severity: Major within F1: the false retained mean directly changes the core adaptive coefficient and EMA; grouped with the startup defect rather than counted as another finding
supporting_count_error.core_dependency: Eq. (11) -> Eq. (12) model factor -> Eqs. (15)-(16) training coefficient, and Eq. (14) next running state. Finite positive-state witness; no reachability from the undefined startup is asserted.

findings.dependency: The undefined dynamic factor is necessary to operate one of the paper's two central proposed mechanisms. This is a substantive method-definition defect without requiring a claim that all experiments fail.
counterevidence: Released implementation uses detached raw gaps, stochastic weighted selection and a mean-of-sigmoids ratio
Released initial model factor is exactly 1
Released selected model statistic averages 12 entries at N=16
No released or historical NaN, training collapse or score reversal demonstrated
findings.repair_verification: Actual retained-count normalization fixes the local mean arithmetic. Full algorithm needs an explicit initialization, gap scale, selection/tie, sigmoid aggregation, EMA, clipping and gradient convention tied to runs. No unique full repair or retraining validated.
findings.later_version: Targeted pre-PMLR arXiv v2 retains relevant formulas and algorithm ordering; its zero-initialization symbol differs, while final PMLR explicitly sets Rbar=0. No later correction located in bounded primary lookup.
